markdown_report:
The best initial experiment is **attribute-sensitive HSTU with a conservative negative curriculum**. It targets broad-but-unspecific recommendations and explicit format/connector mismatches, while testing the measured Electronics separation weakness. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics negatives beat positives at 10.71% of measured positions. This makes negative discrimination a concrete intervention target. (2) Embedding similarity scores near 0.5 imply average cosine similarity near zero. Collapse regularization therefore lacks diagnostic support. (3) Users distinguish detailed relevance from broad association and report compatibility mismatches. Titles/descriptions can supply partial evidence, but cannot establish fulfilled needs or physical compatibility reliably.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Official HSTU configurations demonstrate normalized sampled-softmax training [1]. Their settings provide a reference, not Amazon-specific optimality. (2) R²NS motivates uniform warm-start followed by progressively harder negatives [2]. Stochastic selection may reduce exposure to extreme false negatives. (3) MARS motivates attribute-sensitive representations [3]. Its pretrained machinery cannot transfer directly under this task’s restrictions.

The framework has three directions: **representation specificity**, **negative discrimination**, and **temporal context**. Their corresponding interventions are token features, negative curricula, and HSTU time biases [4]; each remains inside one jointly trained network.

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform 128-negative sampled softmax [1] | 3/6/4/8/2 | Established; scalable; may sharpen related-item ranking; directly tests separation; simple change. | Limited novelty; uncertain transfer; weak compatibility targeting; sampled margins can mislead; sampling exclusions need care. |
| Attribute-sensitive curriculum [2,3], selected | 6/8/8/8/5 | Useful combination; reusable mechanism; targets specificity and format mismatches; challenges confusable negatives; modest encoder. | Components are established; sparse text limits transfer; compatibility remains uncertain; false negatives may hurt; text processing adds complexity. |
| Bucketed temporal attention bias [4] | 3/7/7/5/4 | Native HSTU mechanism; contextual promise; targets stale interests; may clarify context; lightweight parameters. | Low novelty; timing varies; inactivity cannot prove satisfaction; separation benefit is indirect; timestamp alignment requires care. |

**Selected algorithm.** Jointly learn an item-ID embedding plus a small pooled token residual from supplied titles/descriptions, preserving numbers, units and connector tokens. Warm-start HSTU with uniform negatives; subsequently replace a small fraction with stochastic, text-near negatives. Never label explicit attribute differences as proven incompatibility. Exclude known training positives and retain uniform coverage.

Train one checkpoint/category using normalized sampled softmax. Keep seeds, routing, splits, ≤200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch fixed; select solely by macro validation HR@10. Preserve final-nonpadding readout, ModelView interfaces, measured diagnosis definitions, and identical checkpoint/predictor architecture. Compare against the corrected baseline before attributing gains to the proposed mechanism.

idea.description: Train one attribute-sensitive HSTU per category, jointly learning item-ID and lightweight title/description token representations, with uniform warm-start followed by a conservative mixture of uniform and stochastic text-near negatives.
idea.motivation: Address two observed user failures—broad associations replacing specific preferences and recommendations overlooking explicit format/connector distinctions—and the measured Electronics negative-over-positive rate of 10.71%. Available text provides uncertain attribute evidence; it does not establish satisfaction or compatibility.
idea.implementation_notes: Extend the supplied corrected HSTU rather than replacing its backbone. Build vocabulary and text-neighbor proposals from permitted training-side catalog text without pretrained weights or external data. Use one shared item representation and one scoring function, trained jointly and saved in one checkpoint per category. Start with normalized sampled softmax and 128 uniform negatives; after warm-start, test a small text-near fraction such as 25%, sampling stochastically rather than always taking the closest item. Remove padding, the current positive, duplicate negatives, and the user's known training positives. Treat this mixed sampler as a discriminative training objective; do not add an unjustified LogQ correction. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Use the last nonpadding index determined from positions, never nonpadding_count - 1. Serialize text tensors, vocabulary, architecture configuration and learned parameters with the checkpoint; update the embedded predictor writer identically. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView contracts. Report measured margins through predict_score; unavailable category attributes must remain unavailable. No new training or validation results are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each of the four supplied category routes:
    Set training seed to 42; retain supplied preprocessing and splits.
    Construct permitted catalog token tensors and text-neighbor proposals.
    Initialize the corrected HSTU with a jointly trained token residual:
        item_vector(i) = item_emb(i) + projection(mean(token_emb(tokens[i])))
    For epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
        For batch in range(200):
            sequence, positive = family_specific_sample_batch(training_histories)
            negatives = sample_uniform_excluding_known_training_positives()
            If warm_start_complete:
                Replace a small fraction with stochastic text-near negatives.
                Enforce exclusions and deduplicate; refill uniformly if needed.
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            loss = normalized_sampled_softmax(features, positive, negatives)
            Update the single network jointly.
        Use only the supplied validation procedure for checkpoint selection.
    Save one selected checkpoint with architecture and token assets.
Write working/predict.py with the identical model definition and category routing.
At prediction, load exactly one checkpoint for the requested category,
read the final nonpadding feature, and score using the joint item representation.

originality.positive: Combines detailed text features and conservative contextual negative selection inside the existing HSTU under restrictive data and single-model conditions.
originality.negative: The representation and curriculum components are established; novelty lies primarily in the constrained adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable path toward studying which observable item details help sequential models distinguish superficially related choices.
future_potential.negative: Sparse or ambiguous descriptions and false negatives may limit generalization; no validation gain has been demonstrated.

code_difficulty.positive: A small token encoder and static neighbor proposals avoid extra fitted predictors and preserve the HSTU interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful proposal filtering, memory management, and exact checkpoint/predictor consistency.

related_work.title: [1] Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration
contributions: Provides a reference configuration using 128 negatives, normalized embeddings and temperature 0.05.
limitations: Does not establish optimal settings or improvements for the four Amazon categories.

related_work.title: [2] R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-start and progressively harder stochastic negative sampling.
limitations: Hard negatives can harm early learning and may include relevant unobserved items.
The proposed text-neighbor adaptation is not an established result from this work.

related_work.title: [3] MARS
contributions: Motivates attribute-aware representations and matching beyond overall similarity.
limitations: Its pretrained language-model approach is unavailable under this task's constraints.
Attribute similarity does not establish physical compatibility.

related_work.title: [4] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with gated interactions and positional/temporal attention mechanisms.
limitations: Temporal context alone cannot establish whether a purchase fulfilled a need.
Published results do not establish gains for this proposed benchmark adaptation.
